Chapter 4: The Necessity of Self-Reliance and Preparation.
Have you ever noticed how comforting it feels to believe that someone will always be there for you? Parents want to protect their kids from every hurt, and friends make promises to stick together no matter what.
But life... well, it loves to test those promises. Even the closest bonds can’t cover every challenge.
Picture someone facing a sudden crisis—a loss, an illness, a deep betrayal. Sure, having support makes things lighter, but sometimes, there’s just no one who can step in and fix it. You’re left with decisions that only you can make, and consequences you have to carry on your own. In those moments, the real value of self-reliance comes into sharp focus.
Most of us don’t really prepare for these kinds of challenges. We like to think things will sort themselves out, or that someone else will swoop in to handle the tough stuff. But anyone who’s faced real hardship knows: being able to stand on your own isn’t a luxury—it’s absolutely necessary. And you don’t just wake up with that ability. It’s something you build, little by little, through life’s ups and downs, by learning, and yes, by making mistakes.
For women, this need for self-reliance can feel even more urgent. Think about how society sometimes limits opportunities for women—blocking access to education, restricting legal rights, or making it tough to earn their own income. That leaves women vulnerable, relying on others just to get by, and strips away their power to shape their own lives. Not only is that unfair, it’s downright risky.
So, what’s the answer? To really prepare for life’s curveballs, everyone needs the right tools. That means education, the chance to own property, and the freedom to make choices about work, family, and community. It means seeing each person—no matter who they are—as capable of growing, taking responsibility, and even leading.
And here’s something to remember: self-reliance doesn’t mean isolating yourself or putting your needs above everyone else. It’s about having the confidence to face challenges head-on, and the wisdom to ask for help when it matters. When you build that kind of strength, you’re actually making room for more kindness, more compassion, and deeper connections with others.
